title: Luxury Machu Picchu Tours
tagline: La travesía definitiva en Lima, Cusco, Valle Sagrado y Machu Picchu con servicio 5 estrellas.
overview:
Masters of farming, engineering geniuses, and creators of a religion blending animism with nature worship, the Incas remain one of the world’s most fascinating and enigmatic ancient civilizations. Uncover their extraordinary legacy with Unu Raymi Expeditions on one of our luxury Machu Picchu tours, thoughtfully designed to immerse you in Peru’s captivating history and vibrant culture.

These luxury Machu Picchu tours provide a unique opportunity to delve into the remarkable accomplishments of the Incan civilization. From the triumphal constructions of Machu Picchu and the intricate stonework of the old Inca capital Cusco to the ingenious agricultural terraces that dot the stunningly serene Sacred Valley, every element tells a story of ingenuity and vision. Discover the essence of this ancient empire through journeys crafted with sophistication and care.

itinerary.title: DAY 1 - Arrival in Lima
itinerary.subtitle: Arrive at your hotel in Lima after your international flight to Peru!
itinerary.description: You will find us waiting for you when your international flight arrives in Lima. Look for the Unu Raymi sign with your name and smile. We will escort you to your hotel adjacent to the airport, check you in, and help you get settled. You’ll then be able to rinse away the feeling of a long flight and enjoy a good night’s rest!

itinerary.title: DAY 2 - Lima to The Andes
itinerary.subtitle: Fly to Cusco to tour an ancient local hacienda and the Andean countryside.
itinerary.description:
This morning we’ll escort you back to the airport for your morning flight to Cusco. Watch the windows as the desert coast rises into the snow-capped peaks of the Andes!

Just 15 minutes outside of Cusco, true Peruvian countryside will stretch away on either side of you, sheep grazing tranquilly roadside. Impossibly steep peaks rise in the distance. Your journey will take you to an ancient hacienda, nestled in the fertile valley next to the pueblo of Pisac. Step onto the family-owned hacienda grounds and into centuries past while your hosts expound upon the growing process of giant white corn and its profound cultural significance in the Andes Mountains. This hacienda dates back generations, and you’ll immediately be immersed in local customs steeped in the spirits and mysticism of the Andes, embraced by the warmth of local Peruvians.

Relish your time on the farm with a delicious multi-course lunch with dishes featuring none other than the “white gold” giant-kernelled corn, and make sure to visit the on-site stables housing the renowned Peruvian Paso horses. Watch the horses dance with their human counterparts in a “marinera” demonstration and even go for a quick trot yourself if you feel up to the task!

After your meal, we will continue on to your hotel in the Sacred Valley where you can relax surrounded by the beautiful Andes Mountains.

itinerary.title: DAY 3 - Exploring the Sacred Valley
itinerary.subtitle: Private tour of Ollantaytambo and enjoy a traditional Pachamanca feast
itinerary.description:
Today, we will take you to the ancient town of Ollantaytambo, one of the few remaining places in Peru that retains its original Incan urban planning. You’ll note still-functioning street canals, multi-family houses with secret interior courtyards and iconic Incan trapezoidal doors! Here we’ll visit the Incan fortress perched on the mountainside overlooking the sleepy pueblo, and learn about nearby stone quarries and the pivotal Incan battle fought here.

We hope you worked up an appetite this morning, because next on the schedule is a true Peruvian feast: the traditional Pachamanca! The centuries-old Pachamanca tradition involves marinating lamb, pork, chicken, and potatoes in a variety of Andean ingredients and cooking them to perfection in an underground oven. You’ll witness each step of the process: how the oven is prepared, how white-hot stones are layered, and how the feast materializes before your eyes!

While waiting for your feast to roast, make sure to wander through the grounds’ organic garden, smell the fresh-roasted coffee produced by the farm’s head roaster, and sample some of the varieties of cañazo (a local Andean spirit) that are produced on-site at the one-of-a-kind distillery.

Upon completion of your tour, we will bring you back to your hotel for an afternoon spent at leisure in the beautiful Sacred Valley.

itinerary.title: DAY 4 - The Lost City of the Incas
itinerary.subtitle: Morning Hiram Bingham train through the cloud forest / Private tour of Machu Picchu
itinerary.description:
Prepare for a climactic day! In the morning, you will board the luxury Hiram Bingham train for your journey to Machu Picchu. Watch the cloud jungle pass by through the large glass windows and enjoy a gourmet lunch on-board! Make sure to take advantage of the open-air observatory car in this 1920’s Pullman-inspired train.

After a bus ride to the gates of this wonder of the world, you will pass through the main gates with your private guide to finally emerge at the top of the world – Machu Picchu. The incredible Inca stone construction will be spread below, alternately hidden and revealed by clouds. Your expert guide will lead you on a private tour of the ancient city.

Upon conclusion of your tour, return for an evening in Aguas Calientes. Enjoy an excellent dinner on-site at your hotel and fall into bed, lulled to sleep by the sound of the cloud forest around you.

itinerary.title: DAY 5 - Machu Picchu on your terms
itinerary.subtitle: Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at your hotel this morning, and lace up your hiking boots.
itinerary.description:
If you’re feeling adventurous, you can hike up the iconic sugarloaf peak in the background of the classic Machu Picchu postcard photo – Huayna Picchu! Delight in an alternate perspective of Machu Picchu from the top of what is certainly a true feat of engineering.

After a delicious lunch, you will descend to Aguas Calientes for your return Hiram Bingham train. Take advantage of the Belmond waiting room at the train station, and once onboard you’ll be served a gourmet dinner accompanied by live Andean musicians. We will be waiting in the station for you when you arrive and will bring you to your hotel for an evening at leisure.

itinerary.title: DAY 6 - Maras and Moray
itinerary.subtitle: Learn to make Chicha before Exploring Maras and Moray on Horseback
itinerary.description:
Today we enjoy a special day, visiting several treasures of the Sacred Valley of the Incas, off-the beaten path, and away from the crowds.

Surrounded by colorful mountains, hummingbirds, and horses, you will learn and participate hands on how to make Chicha de Jora, the traditional drink of the Incas – a type of delicious and refreshing corn beer. You will also experience the ritual ceremonies that take place when drinking Chicha.

You will then enjoy a lunch of tasty and colorful Peruvian flavors, descending from diverse cultures.

This afternoon, you will enjoy a day of easy horseback riding along the footsteps of the Incas a top the famous Peruvian Paso horses. We will spend approximately 3 ½ hours riding through the mountains, visiting the Maras salt mines, the quaint, colonial village of Maras, and the archeological site of Moray, an agricultural experimentation and development center of the Incas.

From here we begin our return to the ranch, descending through large expanses of farmland, with spectacular views of the mountains and fields. This part of the ride is a beautiful mix of peaceful landscapes and adventurous riding, perfect for all experience levels.

Upon completion of your tour, your private transport will bring you to your hotel in Cusco.

itinerary.title: DAY 7 - Cusco
itinerary.subtitle: Explore the hidden cobblestone streets of historical Cusco on a private city tour!
itinerary.description:
It’s time to get acquainted with Cusco, a gorgeous city that wins the heart of most every traveler that passes through it. Get to know the real Cusco during a private tour. After breakfast, meet your guide and wander among the archaeological remains of Sacsayhuaman, where the Incas staged a great battle against the conquistadors.

Return to the city and roam the atmospheric streets of the bohemian neighborhood of San Blas, which is known for its free-spirited scene. Explore Qoricancha and the Santo Domingo monastery (a colonial structure built on top of the ancient Inca temple of the sun); see where the locals make their grocery runs at the open-air San Pedro market and pass the famous 12-angled stone, whose image appears on the bottle of the local Cusqueña beer.

Upon conclusion of your tour your guide will leave you with suggestions as to where you find a delicious, local lunch, and you’ll have the remainder of the afternoon to explore the Imperial City at your leisure.

itinerary.title: DAY 8 - Cusco to Lima and home
itinerary.subtitle: Fly to Lima – Colonial tour of the capital – Return home
itinerary.description:
This morning, we will escort you to the airport for your flight to Lima. Watch the windows as the snow-capped peaks of the Andes become coastal desert! Your Unu Raymi Lima host will meet you when you touch down in Lima.

Enjoy a ride along the coast as your private driver brings you to the Pueblo Libre neighborhood, home to the Larco Herrera Museum. Housing the country’s largest collection of pre-Columbian artifacts (including extensive gold and silver collections, as well as the infamous erotic archaeological collection) and providing rare open access to their exquisitely catalogued storage area, this museum is the perfect introduction to Peru’s multi-faceted cultural history. First, you’ll begin your visit with a delicious lunch enjoyed on the vine-covered terrace of the Museum’s café, and then you’ll have time to explore the exhibits.

We will take a private tour of Lima that will bring you to the beautiful colonial center of the city. You will visit the Lima Cathedral and the Convent of San Francisco. The catacombs under the convent house the skeletal remains of much of colonial Lima!

We will also visit Casa Aliaga, a 1535 mansion – it is one of the oldest mansions in the New World and has been occupied by the Aliaga family since its construction.

At the appropriate time, we will bring you to the airport for your journey home.

Thank you for traveling with Unu Raymi Expeditions, and buen viaje!

title: Machu Picchu and Amazon Tours
tagline: La perfecta unión entre la mística ciudadela inca y la biodiversidad indómita de la selva.
overview:
Experience a captivating blend of unspoiled wilderness and historic wonders with our Machu Picchu and Amazon tours, where nature and culture converge in unforgettable ways.

This thoughtfully designed itinerary begins in Peru’s Amazon jungle, home to unparalleled biodiversity—one in ten of the world’s known species resides here. After immersing yourself in the rainforest’s wonders, journey to the heart of the Inca Empire. Meet skilled local artisans and playful camelids in the serene Sacred Valley, take in breathtaking views of the jagged Andean peaks, and marvel at the awe-inspiring ancient citadel of Machu Picchu. With these Machu Picchu and Amazon tours, you can expect to explore Cusco, a city where Inca, colonial, and modern influences intertwine, offering a vivid portrayal of Peru’s rich heritage.

itinerary.title: DAY 1 - Arrival in Lima
itinerary.subtitle: Welcome to Peru! Arrive at your hotel in Lima, the City of Kings
itinerary.description: When your flight arrives in Lima, an Unu Raymi host will welcome you personally and escort you to the hotel. Instead of navigating a new city after a long flight, let us take care of the transportation logistics. We will drop you off at your hotel so you can refresh and enjoy a peaceful evening before the adventure truly begins. Relax with a good night’s rest before your flight to Puerto Maldonado in the morning.

itinerary.title: DAY 2 - Lima to Tambopata
itinerary.subtitle: Fly to Puerto Maldonado where the Amazon expedition begins
itinerary.description:
In the morning, your Unu Raymi host will escort you to the airport for a flight to Puerto Maldonado. A travel guide from your jungle hotel will be waiting when you land and captain the boat to the Inkaterra Reserva Amazonica lodge. Upon arrival, you will be served a delicious lunch with fresh-pressed juices.

Embark on a guided jungle walk along the Reserva Amazonica natural area, where you will find Shihuahuaco trees that can grow to the heights of 50 meters (164 feet) and a diameter of 1 meter (3.3 feet) over the course of 700 years. Learn about the strangler fig trees, or matapalos, and spot exotic jungle birds and insects.

As the sun sets, enjoy a twilight tiver excursion watching the jungle transform into an energetic nocturnal world. Spot unique mammals, amphibians, reptiles, and insects that thrive in the darkness, and enjoy their peaceful songs as you fall asleep in the ecolodge.

itinerary.title: DAY 3 - Tambopata Jungle
itinerary.subtitle: Embark on the ultimate jungle excursion
itinerary.description:
After a serene sunrise breakfast, sail to Lake Sandoval, gliding along the Amazon River in a wooden canoe. Voyage a captivating oxbow lake and see if you can spot one of the endangered river otters. Other wild inhabitants here include red howler monkeys, red-bellied macaws, anacondas, sick-neck turtles, and more.

Nourish yourself with an energizing lunch before exploring the Inkaterra Canopy Walkway. Here, you’ll wander across eight observation platforms, located 30 meters high in the jungle canopies, linked by suspension bridges. Be on the lookout for toucans, woodpeckers, trogons, monkeys, and the three-toed sloth. After your descent, stroll along the Anaconda Walk and observe various species of amphibians, birds, mammals, and the lush foliage of this seasonally flooded marshland.

itinerary.title: DAY 4 - Tambopata Jungle
itinerary.subtitle: Trek the dark-water creek and take a daring late-night jungle excursion
itinerary.description:
It’s another early morning today, as you set off to investigate Gamitana creek. Embrace the exciting wildlife research opportunities on this winding dark-water creek, home to piranhas, caiman, turtles, and birds. Afterward, visit Gamitana Model Farm and learn about Amazonian agriculture. You’ll even get the chance to make your own plantain flour used to make bread back at the lodge.

After lunch, it is a 35-minute boat ride upstream to the Hacienda Concepcion – an extraordinary botanical garden with over 200 different species of flora and fauna. After a calming afternoon, prepare for a daring Rainforest by Night experience hosted by the Inkaterra Ecological Reserve. Venture into the forest and spot creatures that only come out to play at night.

itinerary.title: DAY 5 - Tambopata Jungle to Cusco
itinerary.subtitle: Fly to Cusco and travel to the Sacred Valley with stops along the way
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, we will bid goodbye to the Amazon jungle as the Refugio Amazonas team will escort you back to Puerto Maldonado. From the airport, you will embark on a flight to Cusco.

Once you touch down in Cusco, an Unu Raymi host will escort you family to an inviting lunch before taking you to the Sacred Valley. The drive there will be its own adventure as we stop at the Sulca Living Museum, showcasing a comprehensive collection of ancient textile art from various Peruvian cultures. Here, you'll also have the unique opportunity to meet Peru's renowned llamas and alpacas up close!

After your visit, we will bring you to your hotel in the heart of the Sacred Valley for an evening at leisure.

itinerary.title: DAY 6 - Exploring the Sacred Valley
itinerary.subtitle: Private tour of Ollantaytambo and enjoy a traditional Pachamanca feast
itinerary.description:
Start your tour of the Sacred Valley with a visit to the mysterious Ñaupa Iglesia, before continuing on to the ancient town of Ollantaytambo, where the centuries-old influence of the Incas is still very much visible. Water from the mountains trickles down to the Inca-built street canals, while the original Inca walls and trapezoidal doors are still standing.

With your guide by your side, ascend beyond the slope-side terraces to the ruins of a centuries-old fortress above the town. This is the spot where the Incas secured an important victory over the Spanish conquistadors. Inspect the intricately hewn stone constructions and have your guide show you the distant quarries from which the Incas sourced their materials. This site also affords fabulous views of the valley and the Urubamba River that meanders through it.

We hope you worked up an appetite this morning, because next on the schedule is a true Peruvian feast: the traditional Pachamanca! The centuries-old Pachamanca tradition involves marinating lamb, pork, chicken, and potatoes in a variety of Andean ingredients and cooking them to perfection in an underground oven. You’ll witness each step of the process: how the oven is prepared, how white-hot stones are layered, and how the feast materializes before your eyes!

While waiting for your feast to roast, make sure to wander through the grounds’ organic garden, smell the fresh-roasted coffee produced by the farm’s head roaster, and sample some of the varieties of cañazo (a local Andean spirit) that are produced on-site at the one-of-a-kind distillery.

Upon completion of your meal, we will bring you back to your hotel for an afternoon spent at leisure in the beautiful Sacred Valley.

itinerary.title: DAY 7 - The Lost City of the Incas
itinerary.subtitle: Morning train through the cloud forest on your way to visit Machu Picchu!
itinerary.description:
This is the moment all Peruvian explorers wait for. Board the train in Ollantaytambo to begin your Machu Picchu journey. Watch the cloud jungle pass by through the large glass windows, and see if you can spot some alpacas grazing in the valley! When you arrive in Aguas Calientes, enjoy an early lunch before ascending to the lost Incan citadel.

After a bus ride to the gates of South America’s most notable wonder, you will finally emerge at the top of the world – Machu Picchu. The incredible Inca stone citadel will reveal itself to you as you enter the main gates, a city intertwined with the clouds. Your expert guide will give you a private tour of the ancient city.

Upon conclusion of your tour, return for an evening in Aguas Calientes. Enjoy an excellent dinner on-site at your hotel and fall into bed, lulled to sleep by the sound of the cloud forest around you.

itinerary.title: DAY 8 - Machu Picchu on your terms
itinerary.subtitle: Embark on an exclusive trek up the highly coveted Huayna Picchu!
itinerary.description:
Today you have the option to hike two different trails – Huayna Picchu or Machu Picchu Mountain, so it’s completely up to you! This will be the culmination of your Machu Picchu luxury tour, so enjoy it however you want. Adventurous travelers who desire something off-the-beaten-path should hike the steep slope of Huayna Picchu, offering unrivaled views of Machu Picchu. Please note that only a limited amount of hikers are allowed to climb Huayna Picchu each day and tickets will need to be purchased in advance along with your Machu Picchu entrance.

In the afternoon, reconvene in Aguas Calientes and board the return train to Ollantaytambo. Your Unu Raymi host will meet you at the station and bring you to your hotel for a well-earned evening of rest.

itinerary.title: DAY 9 - Cusco
itinerary.subtitle: Uncover the secrets of Cusco’s cobblestone streets on a private city tour
itinerary.description:
Prepare to fall in love with Cusco, a gorgeous city that wins the heart of almost every traveler that passes through it. A private tour is the best way to learn about this historic city, and get the best insider secrets! After breakfast, meet your guide and wander among the archaeological remains of Sacsayhuaman, where the Incas staged a great battle against the conquistadors. Return to the city and venture through the bohemian neighborhood of San Blas, a hub of artistic inspiration. Explore Qoricancha and the Santo Domingo monastery, a colonial structure built on top of the ancient Inca temple of the sun. Live like a local and grab some groceries in the open-air San Pedro market for a delightful shopping experience!

At the end of the tour, your guide will suggest a few places to enjoy a delicious lunch and take advantage of an afternoon on your terms.

itinerary.title: DAY 10 - Cusco to Lima and Home
itinerary.subtitle: Tour the bohemian streets of Barranco and bid farewell to Peru
itinerary.description: Going home is the worst part of any private Peru vacation, but at Unu Raymi, we’ll do our best to make it as smooth and hassle-free as possible. First, we’ll bring you to Cusco airport for your return flight to Lima. In Lima, an Unu Raymi host will meet you and take you to the seaside bohemian district of Barranco. See the streets of Barranco come alive as you visit a number of local art galleries and shops that support local artisans. Finally, enjoy a first-class gourmet meal featuring world-renowned Peruvian flavors in a restaurant of your choice before returning to the airport for your journey home! Buen Viaje!

Relish jaw-dropping views of the jagged Andean Mountains and soak in the serene atmosphere of Peru’s Sacred Valley. Along the way, meet local inhabitants, from skilled traditional craftspeople to charming camelids. This unforgettable Inca Trail to Machu Picchu journey offers the opportunity to marvel at Machu Picchu and explore some of the region’s other remarkable Inca ruins.

itinerary.title: DAY 2 - Lima to Cusco

itinerary.description:

We will be waiting for you when you touch down at our Andean airport and will bring you to the historic city center of Cusco for a delicious lunch. Afterwards you’ll have the afternoon free to explore and acclimate to the altitude at your own pace.

This evening, you will have your briefing for your Inca Trail!

itinerary.title: DAY 3 - The Sacred Valley
itinerary.description:
This morning, spend a special hour on horseback, away from the crowds and losing yourself in the stunning views of the rural Sacred Valley. After a safety briefing and meeting your horse, we’ll show you our neighborhood, a beautiful section of the Sacred Valley that just a few get to see. There are no popular tourist attractions on this route, which is why this is an unforgettable and peaceful way to experience rural life in the Sacred Valley.

Then for lunch, you’ll experience a traditional Pachamanca! The pachamanca is a culinary tradition that dates back to the Incas as a way to celebrate and pay respect to the Pachamama or Mother Earth, a deity representing fertility to the indigenous people in Peru. The Pachamanca is a real feast that plays a key role in gatherings in different regions of Peru.

Thie afternoon, you will get your hands dirty and learn all about the building traditions of the Sacred Valley with an adobe making workshop. Surrounded by colorful mountains, our local experts in mud brick making will share their first-hand knowledge about this building tradition. With their help, you’ll make some strong mud mix yourself!

After getting cleaned up, we will bring you to your hotel for an afternoon at leisure in the beautiful Sacred Valley.

itinerary.title: DAY 4 - Cusco
itinerary.description:
Prepare to fall in love with Cusco, a gorgeous city that wins the heart of almost every traveler that passes through it. A private tour is the best way to learn about this historic city and uncover the best insider secrets. Your guide will meet you at your hotel, and from there you’ll start your exploration of the city!

Explore the archaeological remains of Sacsayhuaman, where the Incas staged a great battle against the conquistadors, the bohemian neighborhood of San Blas, a hub of artistic inspiration, and Qoricancha and the Santo Domingo monastery, a colonial structure built on top of the ancient Inca temple of the sun, enjoying local snacks and tasty treats along the way!

At the end of the tour, you will be free to explore our vibrant city on your own, and pick up any last minute items so that you will be ready to start your trek in the morning!

itinerary.title: DAY 5 - Inca Trail
itinerary.subtitle: Start your journey on the Inca Trail
itinerary.description:
Prepare to discover why this is one of the world’s most noteworthy hiking routes, winding through several different ecological areas, from the high deserts to tropical rain forests. Not to mention its mysterious archaeological sites, whose covering of jungle overgrowth gives the impression that you are discovering them for the first time. Of course, the Inca Trail saves its greatest reward for last, culminating at the lost city of the Incas: Machu Picchu.

With Unu Raymi, your Inca Trail experience will be a safe and memorable one. You’ll be accompanied by experienced guides and aided by support staff, who will ensure your trek is comfortable and pleasant. Local porters will help you with your luggage and you’ll be provided with delicious, hearty meals to help you keep your energy levels up. We’re also happy to include portable hot showers and massage services upon request – a luxurious way to revive weary trekkers.

Your journey starts when we escort you to the trek’s starting point (point km 82) where you’ll meet your porters. Hike the first section of the trail, weaving through semi-arid terrain along the rushing Urubamba River, providing magnificent views of the looming snowcapped mountains.

We will leave the Urubamba Valley and set off up the Cusichaca River (“Happy Legs River” in Quechua), to our first campsite in Ayapata at 10,829 feet above sea level. This evening, enjoy a wonderful hot dinner prepared by your porters and fall asleep under the stars in the comfort of your tent.

itinerary.title: DAY 6 - Inca Trail
itinerary.subtitle: Facing “Dead Woman’s Pass” during day two on the trail
itinerary.description:
Get ready for a significant challenge today. Get your energy levels up with a hearty breakfast before beginning the ascent up the Warmihuañusca pass (or “Dead Woman’s Pass”), which has an elevation of 13,829 feet above sea level. This name is given due to the crests resembling the form of a woman’s supine body when seen from the valley below.

It will be a challenging 4-hour climb through different microclimates, but you can take plenty of scenic breaks along the way. Stop and settle into your second campsite, Chaquicocha, located at 11,800 feet.

Tonight as you relax in your campsite, revel in today’s accomplishments, as you have completed the most difficult section of the trail.

itinerary.title: DAY 8 - Final Day on the Inca Trail
itinerary.subtitle: Your triumphant arrival at the Sun Gate overlooking Machu Picchu
itinerary.description:
After a very early breakfast, you will head to the checkpoint, say goodbye to your team of porters and chefs, and continue on the journey to the Sun Gate (Inti Punku). From Sun Gate, stare in awe at the horizon, with unparalleled views of the mountains and Machu Picchu. Take a deep breath of relief and triumph as you have tread in the footsteps of the Incas, conquering the historic Inca Trail!

Venture into the lost citadel and take a moment to stop and truly appreciate this staggering ancient site. After ample time exploring this majestic site, make your way to Aguas Calientes by bus and enjoy the rest of the evening relaxing to the sound of the cloud forest around you.

itinerary.title: DAY 9 - Machu Picchu on your terms
itinerary.subtitle: Embark on an exclusive trek up the highly coveted Huayna Picchu!
itinerary.description:
Today you have the option to hike two different trails – Huayna Picchu or Machu Picchu Mountain, depending on which you decide! This will be the culmination of your Machu Picchu luxury tour, so enjoy it however you want.

Adventurous travelers who desire something off-the-beaten-path should hike the steep slope of Huayna Picchu, offering unrivaled views of Machu Picchu. Please note that only a limited number of hikers are allowed to climb Huayna Picchu or Machu Picchu Mountain each day and tickets will need to be purchased well in advance along with your Machu Picchu entrance.

In the afternoon, descend to Aguas Calientes and board the return train to Ollantaytambo. Your Unu Raymi host will meet you at the station and bring you to your hotel in Cusco for a well-earned evening of rest.

itinerary.title: DAY 10 - Cusco to Lima
itinerary.subtitle: Luxuriate with some well-deserved downtime in Cusco and Lima
itinerary.description: This morning, you can continue your exploration of the city of Cusco, or have a relaxing morning in the comforts of your hotel! In the afternoon, we will bring you to the Cusco airport for your return flight to Lima. You will have the evening to spend as you please in the culinary capital of South America.

itinerary.title: DAY 11 - Lima and Home
itinerary.subtitle: Tour the bohemian streets of Barranco and bid farewell to Peru.
itinerary.description:
Going home is the worst part of any private Peru vacation, but at Unu Raymi, we’ll do our best to make it as smooth and hassle-free as possible.

After breakfast, your guide will meet you and take you to the seaside bohemian district of Barranco. See the streets of Barranco come alive as you visit a number of local art galleries and shops that support local artisans. Finally, enjoy a first-class gourmet meal featuring world-renowned Peruvian flavors in a restaurant of your choice before returning to the airport for your journey home. Buen Viaje!

overview_lead: Venture into the heart of the ancient Inca Empire as you challenge yourself to complete the legendary Inca Trail to Machu Picchu. Walk along the same trails once traversed by the Inca people and rediscovered by Hiram Bingham.

Follow in the footsteps of the Incas and enter the ancient kingdom of Machu Picchu through the Sun Gate.
Explore the rural life of the Sacred Valley on horseback.
Embark on a private city tour of Cusco, whose fascinating streets feature a unique concoction of Inca ruins and colonial constructions.
Scale the ancient stone stairway up Machu Picchu’s neighboring peak, Huayna Picchu or Machu Picchu Mountain.
Discover the delights of Peruvian cuisine at the country’s finest dining establishments.
Stay at your choice of boutique and sustainable accommodations throughout your luxury tour of Peru.
Get your hands dirty learning to make traditional adobe bricks.

title: Salkantay Trek to Machu Picchu
tagline: Ruta de expedición virgen bajo la mirada del Apu Salkantay (6,271 m).
overview:
Uncover the secrets of Machu Picchu with a hidden gem excursion retracing the original Inca path stemming from Cusco. Discover the scenic route to this Incan citadel by embarking on a trek to Machu Picchu along the lesser-known Salkantay Trail.

Treasure the experience of a trek to Machu Picchu with this magical alternative to the Inca Trail. Your adventure through the Andes begins in the serene Sacred Valley, where you can immerse yourself in local traditions. Mingle with the welcoming inhabitants—both the kind-hearted locals and the adorable animals—and delve into the world of the Incas. Finally, take on the Salkantay Trek, leading you to the pinnacle of Peru’s bucket-list destinations: the legendary trek to Machu Picchu.

An Unu Raymi host to assist you in every location
The majority of meals in the itinerary

itinerary.title: DAY 1 - Arrival in Lima
itinerary.subtitle: Welcome to Peru! Arrive at your hotel in Lima, the City of Kings.
itinerary.description: When your flight arrives in Lima, an Unu Raymi host will welcome you personally and escort you to the hotel. Instead of navigating a new city after a long flight, let us take care of the transportation logistics. We will drop you off at your hotel so you can refresh and enjoy a peaceful evening before the real excursion starts. Relax with a good night’s rest before your flight to Cusco in the morning.

itinerary.title: DAY 2 - Lima to Cusco
itinerary.subtitle: Fly over the Andes into Cusco
itinerary.description:
You will wake up refreshed and enjoy a complimentary breakfast in your hotel before we escort you back to the airport for your morning flight to Cusco. Watch the windows as the desert coast rises into the snow-capped peaks of the Andes!

We will be waiting for you when you touch down at our Andean airport and will bring you to the historic city center of Cusco for a delicious lunch. Afterwards you’ll have the afternoon free to explore and acclimate to the altitude at your own pace.

This evening, you will have your briefing for your Salkantay Trek.

itinerary.title: DAY 3 - The Sacred Valley
itinerary.subtitle: Explore the Sacred Valley with an excursion through Pisac’s archaeological complexes.
itinerary.description:
This morning, you will start with a life experience through the exploration of the ancestral sounds used by the Incas and pre-Hispanic cultures in various contexts, encouraging the appreciation of these sounds. With this activity you will have the opportunity to learn about and understand the different sounds of pre-Hispanic wind instruments such as: whistles for meditation, communication, ceremonial and ritual purposes. You will also listen to the sounds of some instruments such as: the pututo, whistling vessels, the kero, mancha and puito that were used in Inca and pre-Inca cultures.

Your journey will continue to an ancient hacienda, nestled in the fertile valley next to the pueblo of Pisac. Step onto the family-owned hacienda grounds and step into centuries past while your hosts expound upon the growing process of Giant White Corn and its profound cultural significance in the Andes Mountains. Relish your time on the farm with a delicious multi-course lunch with sample dishes featuring none other than the “white gold” giant-kernelled corn.

Next, you’ll travel up the mountain in your private vehicle for today’s final stop at the ruins overlooking Pisac. Here, you’ll learn about the complexity of the Incan agricultural system, their methods of cultivating thousands of varieties of corn and potatoes, and you’ll watch the sun sink over the tips of the Andes Mountains surrounding you.

Upon completion we’ll return to your hotel in Cusco for an evening at leisure.

itinerary.title: DAY 4 - Cusco
itinerary.subtitle: Uncover the secrets of Cusco’s cobblestone streets with a private city tour.
itinerary.description:
Prepare to fall in love with Cusco, a gorgeous city that wins the heart of almost every traveler that passes through it. A private tour is the best way to learn about this historic city and uncover the best insider secrets. Your guide will meet you at your hotel, and from there you’ll start your exploration of the city! Explore the archaeological remains of Sacsayhuaman, where the Incas staged a great battle against the conquistadors, the bohemian neighborhood of San Blas, a hub of artistic inspiration, and Qoricancha and the Santo Domingo monastery, a colonial structure built on top of the ancient Inca temple of the sun, enjoying local snacks and tasty treats along the way!

At the end of the tour, you will be free to explore our vibrant city on your own, and pick up any last minute items so that you will be ready to start your trek in the morning!

itinerary.title: DAY 5 - Salkantay Trek
itinerary.subtitle: Start your journey on the Salkantay Trek
itinerary.description:
After an early breakfast, you’ll be picked up from your hotel in Cusco and start the drive to the beginning of the trail. Cruise through the purple and blue mountains of the Andes, where you will visit the Tarawasi Incan ruins before reaching Marcoccasa. Here, you will begin your trek on the “Camino Real.” It will be a few hours of hiking today before reaching your first lodge, the Salkantay Lodge and Adventure Resort in Soraypampa.

Salkantay Lodge takes its name from the majestic peak at the head of the valley, Mt. Salkantay. Eternally topped with a covering of snow, Salkantay’s 20,600-foot summit is the highest in the region, and is often obscured by the swirling clouds that rise from the jungle. For the Incas, it was one of the most sacred mountains. You’ll be given a charming Peruvian welcome to the lodge before enjoying dinner.

Sleep overnight at the lodge, which – at 12,690 feet – is a good place to acclimatize to the thinner air.

itinerary.title: DAY 6 - Salkantay Trek
itinerary.subtitle: Relax and enjoy Soraypampa before the real hiking begins
itinerary.description: Today is all about rest and relaxation in the breathtakingly beautiful Humantay Lake, only half an hour from the lodge. This blissful four-hour excursion will be a leisurely way to enjoy the landscape before an evening at the lodge. Take a dip in the outdoor Jacuzzi, and prepare for the next few days of rigorous hiking.

itinerary.title: DAY 7 - Salkantay Trek
itinerary.subtitle: Reach the highest point of the trek at Vilcabamba Range
itinerary.description:
Today, the challenge begins! Your adventure has a mesmerizing start, as you begin the trek with the sunrise illuminating the Andean peaks. Hike to the Rio Blanco valley, circling Humantay Peak across from the summit of Salkantay. Once we reach the highest point on the trek, Salkantay Pass, we’ll take a break. At 15,213 feet, the views from here are glorious. The white-hatted Vilcabamba Range extends in every direction and the glacial south face of Salkantay towers above. Be on alert for Andean condors zooming by; these majestic birds are often seen soaring around the rocky ledges.

From the pass, we’ll descend toward Wayra Lodge, our destination for the night. ‘Wayra’ means wind, and references the nearby Wayracmachay, literally the “place where the wind lives.” Hikers will be given ample sustenance, with a hot picnic lunch served en route and dinner at the lodge.

itinerary.title: DAY 8 - Salkantay Trek
itinerary.subtitle: Descend into the cloud forest and enjoy a Pachamanca feast
itinerary.description:
Being your morning with breakfast at Wayra Lodge before continuing the descent along the left bank of the Salkantay River. The further you plunge, the more verdant the scenery becomes. As the warm air from the jungle rises to envelop you, so do the colorful creatures that thrive in warmer climes: intricately patterned butterflies flutter through the air and attractive orchids can be seen spurting up from the ground.

The destination for today is Colpa Lodge, a charming lodge set on an open plateau at the confluence of three rivers. Once we get there, you and your fellow hungry hikers can fill up on Pachamanca – a traditional Peruvian meal made by layering meat and vegetables with hot stones and cooking them in a covered earthen pit. After, you might want to soothe your shaky calves with a soak in the outdoor Jacuzzi and enjoy the panoramic views. Or, should you crave something a little more active, you can ramble along the nearby orchid trail. Dinner will be at the lodge.

itinerary.title: Day 9 - Salkantay Trek
itinerary.subtitle: Trek past rural farms and explore small villages following the Santa Teresa river valley
itinerary.description:
Today, your luxury Salkantay trek to Machu Picchu continues, hiking across the more populated Santa Teresa River valley. You’ll see evidence of how local valley dwellers make their living. As you pass through plantations, you may even see the community members tending their crops of banana, granadilla, avocado, and coffee. Caffeine enthusiasts may be interested to know that some of the best organic coffees in the world are produced in this very valley!

Come lunchtime, we’ll find a suitable spot to stop by the river and refuel with a hot picnic. After lunch, get moving again for another hour or so until a private vehicle comes to collect us for a quick 30-minute transfer to the beginning of the Llactapata Inca Trail.

Tucked into the mountainside among a lush avocado orchard is our next overnight stop: the Lucma Lodge which will provide dinner and rest before the finale of your trek: Machu Picchu.

itinerary.title: Day 10 - Salkantay Trek
itinerary.subtitle: Get your first glimpse at Machu Picchu and arrive in Aguas Calientes
itinerary.description:
Today you’ll tackle the last day of your trek. The first few hours will be an uphill slog toward Llactapata Pass which gifts travelers with a first look at Machu Picchu in the distance. From this vantage point, you’ll see the site looming from the southeast.

After gazing at the ruins, take some time out to check out the Llactapata ruins, which were also “discovered” by Hiram Bingham on that fateful expedition in 1911. The site, which was recently restored, looks better than ever. Sit down for lunch at a scenic outlook that offers views of Machu Picchu and the surrounding mountains.

Once lunch concludes, begin your descent towards the Urubamba River, passing through several picturesque landscapes comprised of bamboo forests, orchards, and plantations. From here, you’ll ride the train to Aguas Calientes, the closest settlement to Machu Picchu and your final overnight destination before exploring Machu Picchu properly tomorrow. Celebrate your completion of the Salkantay Trail over an indulgent dinner.

itinerary.title: Day 11 - The Lost City of the Incas
itinerary.subtitle: Tour the Machu Picchu Citadel with your expert guide
itinerary.description:
Today will be a day that remains permanently etched in your mind, long after you’ve returned from your personalized trip to Peru, for today will be the day you finally set eyes on the storied city of Machu Picchu!

After an early breakfast at your hotel, meet your guide and begin the bus ride up switchbacks to the Lost Citadel. As you trek up the entrance’s stone steps, heavy foliage hides the surrounding views until you emerge at what seems like the top of the world, with Machu Picchu spread out below. Take in the wonder of this historic, sacred site, relishing in your accomplishment of trekking the valley below. Return to Aguas Calientes for a late lunch, before heading back to your return train to Ollantaytambo.

itinerary.title: Day 12 - Exploring Ollantaytambo and its Secrets
itinerary.description:
Today, you will explore the ancient town of Ollantaytambo, one of the few remaining places in Peru that retains its original Incan urban planning. You’ll note still-functioning street canals, multi-family houses with secret interior courtyards and iconic Incan trapezoidal doors! Here we’ll visit the Incan fortress perched on the mountainside overlooking the sleepy pueblo, and learn about nearby stone quarries and the pivotal Incan battle fought here.

We hope you worked up an appetite this morning, because next on the schedule is a true Peruvian feast: the traditional Pachamanca! The centuries-old Pachamanca tradition involves marinating lamb, pork, chicken, and potatoes in a variety of Andean ingredients and cooking them to perfection in an underground oven. You’ll witness each step of the process: how the oven is prepared, how white-hot stones are layered, and how the feast materializes before your eyes!

While waiting for your feast to roast, make sure to wander through the grounds’ organic garden, smell the fresh-roasted coffee produced by the farm’s head roaster, and sample some of the varieties of cañazo (a local Andean spirit) that are produced on-site at the one-of-a-kind distillery.

At the end of your meal, we will bring you back to Cusco for a final evening at leisure.

This morning, you can continue your exploration of the city of Cusco, or have a lie-in and enjoy the comforts of your hotel! At the appropriate time early this afternoon, we will bring you to the Cusco airport for your return flight to Lima. Your Unu Raymi Lima host will meet you upon arrival and bring you to the Huaca Pucllana site.

Here, you will glimpse pre-Columbian desert ruins, delicately preserved in the middle of Miraflores, one of Lima’s nicest neighborhoods. The huaca, or sacred site, is home to one of Lima’s finest dining establishments where you can enjoy a gourmet meal featuring Peruvian flavors while looking out over some of Lima’s most cherished ruins.

Upon conclusion of your meal, we will bring you to the Lima airport for your journey home. Thank you for traveling with Unu Raymi Expeditions, and buen viaje!

highlights: Take the road less traveled by hiking the Salkantay trek to Machu Picchu, an excellent alternative to the Inca Trail.
Wander the Incan capital city of Cusco with your private guide, discovering local highlights and hidden treasures.
Delight in luxury trek amenities, such as deluxe lodges, jacuzzis, and nightly massages.
Relish a luxury tour of Machu Picchu with a private, expert guide to explain the history and mystery of the site.
Discover the delights of Peruvian cuisine at the country’s finest dining establishments.
Immerse yourself in local life with visits to remote Andean villages that are, for most travelers, uncharted territory.
Enjoy enriching experiences and Sounds of the Andes with local artists and musicians in their element.
Visit the old hacienda of Sarapampa dedicated to local agriculture and enjoy a lovely culinary experience.

title: The Lares Trek Unveiled
tagline: Inmersión íntima en comunidades tejedoras andinas y senderos solitarios.
overview:
The Lares Trek offers a rare window into Peru’s living Andean culture, where remote mountain communities, ancient traditions, and breathtaking landscapes come together in a deeply personal journey.

Along the trail, you will encounter farming villages, traditional weaving practices, herds of llamas and alpacas, and the quiet rhythms of daily life in the high Andes. From the Sacred Valley to the thermal springs of Lares, the waterfalls of Kiswarani, and the remote village of Cancha Cancha, each day reveals a more intimate side of Peru, where Inca heritage and contemporary Andean life continue to shape one another.

An Unu Raymi host to assist you in every location
The majority of meals in the itinerary
Daily activities and excursions as indicated in the itinerary

itinerary.title: DAY 1 - Welcome to Peru!
itinerary.subtitle: International Arrival in Lima
itinerary.description:
You will find us waiting for you when your international flight arrives in Lima. Look for the Unu Raymi sign with your name and the smile. We will escort you to your hotel, check you in, and help you get settled. You’ll then be able to enjoy the afternoon at leisure.

•• Lima is a worldly, bustling metropolis at sea level. From about May through October, Lima’s weather is often overcast with mild temperatures (60–70 degrees Fahrenheit, or 15–21 degrees Celsius), but during the summery months of November through April, be prepared for temperatures upwards of 90 degrees Fahrenheit (32+ Celsius), strong sun, and plenty of humidity.

itinerary.title: DAY 2 - Journey to the Andes
itinerary.subtitle: Flight from Lima to Cusco / Private Car to the Sacred Valley
itinerary.description:
You will wake up refreshed and enjoy a complimentary breakfast in your hotel before we escort you back to the airport for your morning flight to Cusco. Watch the windows as the desert coast rises into the snow-capped peaks of the Andes!

We will be waiting for you when you touch down at our Andean airport and will bring you to the historic city center of Cusco for a delicious lunch. Then, before you can feel the altitude, we’ll whisk you into the Sacred Valley.

Just 15 minutes outside of Cusco, true Peruvian countryside will stretch away on either side of you, cows and sheep grazing tranquilly roadside. Impossibly steep peaks rise in the distance.

Your journey will take you first to the Sulca Living Museum, where you’ll see traditional weavers ply their trade and get to meet Peru’s famous llamas and alpacas face to face. Next, you’ll stop at the vibrant market in the pueblo of Pisac, where locals come from miles around to sell their wares.

Upon conclusion of your market visit, we’ll bring you to your hotel in the heart of the Sacred Valley.

itinerary.title: DAY 3 - The Past, Present, and Future of the Sacred Valley
itinerary.subtitle: Private Tour of Chinchero, Exploration of Tiobamba and the Ruins at Moray
itinerary.description:
Today you will weave through the Sacred Valley’s most fertile agricultural lands and experience an unforgettable blend of the past, present, and future. Your first stop of the day will be the picturesque town of Chinchero, known for its rich cultural heritage and breathtaking Andean landscapes. Explore the impressive archaeological site, which includes well-preserved Inca terraces, colonial-era structures built atop Inca foundations, and a charming 17th-century church decorated with beautiful frescoes.

You’ll also have the opportunity to observe local artisans at work, preserving traditional weaving techniques passed down through generations. From here, you’ll head straight to the charming village of Tiobamba, where a delicious private lunch awaits at the T’asra Room of Unu Restaurant. Enjoy a peaceful meal with spectacular views of Tiobamba’s plaza and the surrounding Sacred Valley mountains. After lunch, visit the remarkable Inca ruins of Moray. These mysterious circular terraces are believed by some archaeologists to have served as an agricultural laboratory, although their true purpose remains uncertain. As you explore this fascinating site, feel free to form your own theory while admiring the ingenuity and craftsmanship of ancient Inca engineering.

Finally, after immersing yourself in the living history of the Sacred Valley, where the past, present, and future of Andean culture converge, we’ll take you to your hotel for a well-deserved evening of rest.

itinerary.title: DAY 4 - Soak in Hot Springs and Reach Your Campsite Under the Falls
itinerary.subtitle: Lares Hot Springs – Kiswarani Waterfall Campsite
itinerary.description:
Today marks the beginning of your Lares Trek adventure. After an early departure, journey into the Lares Valley where you'll enjoy the region’s famous thermal baths before beginning your trek.

The trail leads through traditional farming communities where potatoes have been cultivated for generations. Along the way, your guide will share insights into local customs, medicinal plants, and rural Andean life.

After lunch in Kiswarani, you will have the opportunity to interact with local families and learn about the importance of llamas in Andean culture before continuing to your scenic campsite beneath the waterfalls.

itinerary.title: DAY 5 - Summit Condor Pass and Explore a Traditional Andean Village
itinerary.subtitle: Kiswarani – Condor Pass – Cancha Cancha
itinerary.description:
Wake to spectacular views of the surrounding mountains and begin the ascent toward Condor Pass, the highest point of the trek.

Along the route, enjoy breathtaking panoramas of alpine lakes, waterfalls, llamas, and alpacas grazing across the mountainsides. Upon reaching the pass, you'll be rewarded with sweeping views of the Andes and the sacred peak of Pitusiray.

After lunch, descend toward the remote community of Cancha Cancha, one of the few villages where traditional Andean lifestyles remain largely unchanged.

Spend time learning about local customs, weaving traditions, and daily life before enjoying another evening in the mountains.

itinerary.title: DAY 6 - Through Ancient Communities to the Sacred Valley
itinerary.subtitle: Cancha Cancha – Huaran – Maras Salt Mines – Sacred Valley
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, continue descending through beautiful mountain scenery and traditional farming communities.

As the landscape gradually changes from high Andean terrain to the fertile Sacred Valley, you'll gain insight into the agricultural traditions that continue to sustain local families today.

Upon reaching Huaran, bid farewell to your trekking team and continue by vehicle to the remarkable Maras Salt Mines. These thousands of salt pans have been harvested since pre-Inca times and continue to provide a livelihood for local families.

Following your visit, continue to your hotel in the Sacred Valley where a comfortable bed and hot shower await.

itinerary.title: DAY 7 - Discovering the Heart of the Inca Empire
itinerary.subtitle: Private Tour of Cusco’s Historic City Center / Fly from Cusco to Lima / Return Home
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, we will transfer you from the Sacred Valley back to Cusco for a final exploration of the former capital of the Inca Empire.

This morning you will experience the lay of the land as only true world travelers know how: traversing hidden alleyways, historic plazas, and local treasures. Your private guide will illuminate Cusco’s rich tapestry, woven through its inviting cobblestone streets, charming neighborhoods, and astounding landmarks.

You’ll stop at the colonial Cathedral in the Plaza de Armas, home to an extraordinary collection of religious art and centuries of history. From there, continue to the Santo Domingo Monastery, built atop the most sacred of Incan sites, the Qoricancha Temple of the Sun. Once bathed in sheets of gold before the arrival of the Spanish, this remarkable site is now an astounding blend of Incan stonemasonry and colonial architecture.

Next, visit the San Pedro Market, one of the most vibrant and traditional markets in Cusco. Designed by Gustave Eiffel and opened in 1925, this bustling market offers an authentic glimpse into everyday Andean life. As you wander through its colorful stalls, you’ll find everything from fresh produce, meats, and cheeses to local handicrafts, textiles, and herbal remedies. It’s a wonderful place to experience the flavors, aromas, and culture of the region, and perhaps enjoy a freshly blended juice or pick up a handmade souvenir.

Finally, travel by private vehicle to the impressive Sacsayhuaman archaeological complex overlooking the city. Here, marvel at the colossal stone walls and learn about the strategic and ceremonial importance of one of the greatest achievements of Inca engineering.

At the appropriate time, we will bring you to the Cusco airport for your flight to Lima and onward international connection home.

Thank you for traveling with Unu Raymi Expeditions, and buen viaje!

title: Luxury Huayhuash Trek
tagline: La cordillera más sobrecogedora de los Andes peruanos recorrida con máximo confort.
overview:
Embark on a luxury Huayhuash trek through one of the most spectacular and remote mountain ranges in the Andes, where turquoise lakes, high-altitude passes, and snow-capped peaks define every step of the journey.

Your adventure begins in Huaraz, with private acclimatization hikes to glacial lakes such as Willcacocha and Churup before setting out on the legendary Cordillera Huayhuash circuit. Over several days, you will cross dramatic passes above 5,000 meters, camp beneath the iconic peaks of Yerupajá and Siula, and experience the raw majesty of the remote Andes with the full support of your private guide and dedicated mountain crew.

itinerary.title: DAY 2 - Hello Huaraz
itinerary.subtitle: Flight to Huaraz / Private Transfer to Anta
itinerary.description:
You will wake up refreshed and enjoy a complimentary buffet breakfast in the hotel before returning to the airport for your morning flight to Huaraz. Watch the windows as the desert coast rises into the snow-capped peaks of the Andes.

We will be waiting for you when you touch down at our small Andean airport. Then, we will bring you to your hotel in the town of Anta, about an hour away.

You will have the rest of the day to rest and explore as you see fit! The hotel staff will be able to point you in the direction of some nearby trails for some light hiking.

itinerary.title: DAY 3 - Willcacocha Lake
itinerary.subtitle: Private Excursion & Hike to Willcacocha Lake
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, you will meet your private driver & guide and head out towards Willcacocha.

This lagoon is located in the Cordillera Negra, about 50 minutes southwest of Huaraz at 3,470 m.a.s.l. In this place, we can see the entire Cordillera Blanca and peaks such as Huandoy, Huascarán, Chopicalqui, Hualcán, Copa, Vallunaraju, Ocshapalca, Ranrapalca, and Palcaraju.

Depending on how you are feeling, you will have the option to hike to the lake (about an hour and a half).

Afterward, there will be a short 30-minute walk to the town of Santa Cruz, where your driver will be waiting to take you back to your hotel. (Massage included for this evening.)

itinerary.title: DAY 4 - Churup Lake
itinerary.subtitle: Private Excursion & Hike to Churup Lake
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, you will meet your private driver & guide and head east along a road passing through Andean villages to Pitec, approximately one hour away.

You will experience the splendid views of Vallunaraju (5,686 m.a.s.l.), Ocshapalca (5,881 m.a.s.l.), Ranrapalca (6,162 m.a.s.l.), Rimarima (5,203 m.a.s.l.), Churup (5,495 m.a.s.l.), San Juan (5,843 m.a.s.l.), Huamashraju (5,434 m.a.s.l.), Cayesh (5,728 m.a.s.l.), and Huantsan (6,113 m.a.s.l.).

Once in Pitec, you will begin the ascent to Churup Lake at the base of Mount Churup. The hike takes approximately three hours. Upon arrival at the lake, you will have time for a short walk to the northern lakeshore.

You will then return to Pitec along the same trail, where your driver will be waiting to take you back to your hotel. (Massage included for this evening.)

itinerary.title: DAY 5 - In the Footsteps of Giants
itinerary.subtitle: Travel to the First Camp of the Huayhuash (Approximately Six Hours Drive)
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, you will head south with your private guide and driver, where the snow-capped peaks of the Cordillera Blanca can be seen from Pachacoto (35 km).

You will then continue east across a wild puna landscape and visit the Puya de Raimondi. The Huayhuash Range, containing seven of the highest and most dramatic summits in Peru, gradually reveals itself as we descend toward the small town of Chiquián.

Camp will be in Cuartelhuaín (3,900 m.a.s.l.), near the Rondoy Valley, from where you will appreciate your first views of the magnificent Cordillera Huayhuash summits.

itinerary.title: DAY 6 - Day 1 on the Huayhuash Trail
itinerary.subtitle: Cuartelhuaín – Mitucocha – Carhuacocha (4,100 m)
itinerary.description:
From Cuartelhuaín, we begin the circular walk around the Cordillera Huayhuash. Here we will meet our mountain crew, including cooks, muleteers, and support staff, before beginning the trek.

Once the donkeys have been loaded, we begin the ascent to cross the first pass, Cacananpunta (4,700 m.a.s.l.), where the mountains fill the landscape. We then descend through a wide and grassy valley across to the beautiful Mitucocha Lake (4,200 m.a.s.l.), where we set up camp along the lakeshore.

We will then take an afternoon walk alongside the moraine toward Ninancocha Lake (4,400 m.a.s.l.) at the foot of Jirishanca and Rondoy. We continue ascending the Mitucocha Valley to Punta Carhuac (4,650 m.a.s.l.), with excellent views of Siula and Yerupajá. We then descend toward the beautiful Carhuacocha Lake, where we set up camp in an excellent broad grassy area beside the lake.

We will spend two nights here with splendid views of Siula, Yerupajá, and Jirishanca.

itinerary.title: DAY 7 - Day 2 on the Huayhuash Trail
itinerary.subtitle: Carhuacocha – Huayhuash (4,350 m)
itinerary.description:
This day can be a free day to rest from the trekking and make an excellent side trip to the beautiful turquoise Siula Lake (4,300 m.a.s.l.) and Quesillococha Lake (4,500 m.a.s.l.), located at the base of Siula’s impressive face.

We begin the walk following the course of the river downstream until the base of the Queropalca Valley. Turning southward, we begin the ascent toward Carnicero Pass (4,600 m.a.s.l.), with excellent mountain views of Yerupajá (6,634 m.a.s.l.), one of the highest peaks in the Peruvian Andes, and Siula (6,344 m.a.s.l.), the famous mountain featured in Joe Simpson’s book Touching the Void .

We enjoy magnificent views of the Carnicero and Trapecio peaks before descending toward the small settlement of Huayhuash, where we set up camp (4,350 m.a.s.l.).

itinerary.title: DAY 8 - Day 3 on the Huayhuash Trail
itinerary.subtitle: Huayhuash – Viconga (4,500 m)
itinerary.description:
Today the trek approaches the southern end of the Cordillera Huayhuash.

We ascend to Huayhuash Pass (4,700 m.a.s.l.) and are rewarded with views of the Cordillera Raura and, on the opposite side, Trapecio Peak. Descending southward, we arrive at Viconga Lake (4,500 m.a.s.l.) and set up camp nearby.

Later, we will walk to the Putcka thermal springs to enjoy a relaxing hot bath before returning to camp.

itinerary.title: Day 9 - Day 4 on the Huayhuash Trail
itinerary.subtitle: Viconga – Huanacpatay (4,200 m)
itinerary.description:
This is the fourth day of walking and one of the longest days of the trek.

Our goal is to cross Cuyoc Pass (5,000 m.a.s.l.), the highest point of the route, from where we enjoy a spectacular panoramic view of the Cordillera Huayhuash.

We then descend into the Huanacpatay Valley, surrounded by larger-than-life Andean peaks, where we set up camp at 4,200 m.a.s.l.

itinerary.title: Day 10 - Day 5 on the Huayhuash Trail
itinerary.subtitle: Huanacpatay – Huayllapa (3,550 m)
itinerary.description:
Today, we begin ascending to San Antonio Pass (5,050 m.a.s.l.). From here, you can enjoy some of the most spectacular views in the Cordillera Huayhuash, highlighting Sarapo, Yerupajá, Jurao, and Siula. The contrast between these towering snow-capped peaks and the turquoise waters of Sarapococha and Jurao Lagoons is nothing short of breathtaking.

Continuing the trek, we descend through Quebrada Huayllapa to reach the village of Huayllapa (3,550 m.a.s.l.), where we briefly stop before beginning our ascent through Quebrada Tapush toward our campsite in Huatia (4,300 m.a.s.l.).

For those who prefer not to ascend to San Antonio Pass, there is the option of continuing directly down to Huayllapa and camping there.

itinerary.title: Day 11 - Day 6 on the Huayhuash Trail
itinerary.subtitle: Huayllapa – Gashpapampa (4,400 m)
itinerary.description:
Today, you will continue ascending toward Tapush Pass (4,800 m.a.s.l.), before descending toward Susococha Lake and our campsite at Gashpapampa (4,400 m.a.s.l.).

This pleasant campsite offers impressive views of Suerococha and Diablo Mudo (Silent Devil), one of the most iconic peaks of the Huayhuash Range.

itinerary.title: Day 12 - Day 7 on the Huayhuash Trail
itinerary.subtitle: Gashpapampa – Jahuacocha (4,050 m)
itinerary.description:
Today you will face the ascent to Suerococha Pass (5,300 m.a.s.l.). Climbing experience is not required, as the route presents no technical difficulties, although conditions may require the use of equipment such as crampons, harnesses, ice axes, ropes, snow boots, and sunglasses depending on the season.

The descent through the Huacrish Valley eventually leads to the stunning Jahuacocha Lake, where we will set up camp along its shores.

Surrounded by some of the most dramatic peaks in the Peruvian Andes, this is one of the most scenic campsites of the entire trek.

itinerary.title: Day 13 - Final Day on the Trail!
itinerary.subtitle: Jahuacocha – Llamac (3,250 m) – Chiquián (3,350 m) – Huaraz
itinerary.description:
This is the final day of trekking through Quebrada Huayllan. You will follow the waters flowing from Jahuacocha Lake while enjoying colorful Andean landscapes, native ichu grasslands, quenual forests, and splendid views of Rondoy, Jirishanca, Yerupajá Chico, and Yerupajá Grande.

We descend along a newly constructed irrigation canal before continuing toward Llamac (3,300 m.a.s.l.), with final views of Diablo Mudo dominating the skyline.

In this last section, we follow a high traverse before arriving in Llamac after approximately four hours of hiking, where our vehicle will be waiting to pick us up and begin the journey back to Huaraz.

We will make a brief stop in the town of Chiquián before continuing to Huaraz, arriving approximately three hours later. Upon arrival at your hotel, enjoy a well-deserved rest and a complimentary massage this evening.

overview_headline: Private Expedition Into The Andean Heart
overview_lead: Embark on a luxury Huayhuash trek through one of the most spectacular and remote mountain ranges in the Andes, where turquoise lakes, high-altitude passes, and snow-capped peaks define every step of the journey.

title: Amazon River Cruise
tagline: Navegue el Amazonas y la Reserva Pacaya Samiria en embarcaciones boutique de 5 estrellas.
overview:
Set sail on a luxury Amazon River cruise, exploring the world’s largest tropical rainforest. Discover vibrant wildlife, lush landscapes, and remote jungle wonders.

Begin with Peru’s iconic sites like Machu Picchu and Cusco. Then, embark on a four-night Amazon River cruise, navigating remote tributaries from Iquitos. Enjoy jungle trekking, piranha fishing, and wildlife watching, from pink dolphins to colorful bird species.
inclusions: Personalized itinerary planning
An Unu Raymi host to assist you in every location
The majority of meals in the itinerary
Daily activities and excursions as indicated in the itinerary
exclusions: International flights to and from your home country

itinerary.title: DAY 1 - Arrival in Lima
itinerary.subtitle: Arrive at your hotel in Lima after your flight to Peru
itinerary.description: When your flight arrives in Lima, an Unu Raymi host will welcome you personally and escort you to the hotel. Instead of navigating a new city after a long flight, let us take care of the transportation logistics. We will drop you off at your hotel so you can refresh and enjoy a peaceful evening before the real excursion starts. Relax with a good night’s rest before your flight to Cusco in the morning.

itinerary.title: DAY 2 - Lima to Cusco
itinerary.subtitle: Fly to Cusco and tour a historic local hacienda and the Peruvian countryside.
itinerary.description:
This morning we’ll escort you back to the airport for your morning flight to Cusco. Watch the windows as the desert coast rises into the snow-capped peaks of the Andes!

Just 15 minutes outside of Cusco, true Peruvian countryside will stretch away on either side of you, sheep grazing tranquilly roadside. Impossibly steep peaks rise in the distance. Your journey will take you to a historic hacienda, nestled in the fertile valley next to the pueblo of Pisac. Step onto the family-owned hacienda grounds and into centuries past while your hosts expound upon the growing process of giant white corn and its profound cultural significance in the Andes Mountains. This hacienda dates back generations, and you’ll immediately be immersed in local customs steeped in the spirits and mysticism of the Andes, embraced by the warmth of local Peruvians.

Relish your time on the farm with a delicious multi-course lunch with dishes featuring none other than the “white gold” giant-kernelled corn, and make sure to visit the on-site stables housing the renowned Peruvian Paso horses. Watch the horses dance with their human counterparts in a “marinera” demonstration and even go for a quick trot yourself if you feel up to the task!

After your meal, we will continue on to your hotel in the Sacred Valley where you can relax surrounded by the beautiful Andes Mountains.

itinerary.title: DAY 3 - Exploring the Sacred Valley
itinerary.subtitle: Hike to Ollantaytambo’s Iconic Ruins & Explore the Arts of the Sacred Valley
itinerary.description:
Journey through the Inca’s Sacred Valley, starting with a drive through the breathtaking Patacancha Valley. After a stop at the ruins of Pumamarca, you will begin the hike down a pre-Columbian trail, following ancient irrigation canals that line terraced fields still in use today.

After approximately two hours of easy hiking, the town of Ollantaytambo will appear, where the influence of the Incas is still very much visible. Water from the mountains trickles down to the Inca-built street canals, while original Inca walls and trapezoidal doors still stand.

With your guide by your side, ascend beyond the slope-side terraces to the ruins of a centuries-old fortress above the town. This is the spot where the Incas secured an important victory over the Spanish conquistadors. Inspect the intricately hewn stone constructions and have your guide show you the distant quarries from which the Incas sourced their materials. This site also affords fabulous views of the valley and the Urubamba River that meanders through it.

Following a lunch featuring local flavors, hop back in the car. This time, we’ll take you to our favorite artist’s workshop, famous throughout Peru for handcrafted ceramics. Spend the afternoon laughing, learning, and creating hand-made souvenirs with a Peruvian flair to bring home with you!

Upon completion of your tour, we will bring you back to your hotel for an evening spent at leisure.

itinerary.title: DAY 4 - The Lost City of the Incas
itinerary.subtitle: Morning train through the cloud forest on your way to visit Machu Picchu
itinerary.description:
This is the moment all Peruvian explorers wait for. Board the train in Ollantaytambo to begin your Machu Picchu journey. Watch the cloud jungle pass by through the large glass windows, and see if you can spot some alpacas grazing in the valley! When you arrive in Aguas Calientes, enjoy an early lunch before ascending to the lost Incan citadel.

After a bus ride to the gates of South America’s most notable wonder, you will finally emerge at the top of the world – Machu Picchu. The incredible Inca stone citadel will reveal itself to you as you enter the main gates, a city intertwined with the clouds. Your expert guide will give you a private tour of the ancient city.

Upon conclusion of your tour, return for an evening in Aguas Calientes. Enjoy an excellent dinner on-site at your hotel and fall into bed, lulled to sleep by the sound of the cloud forest around you.

itinerary.title: DAY 5 - Machu Picchu on your terms
itinerary.subtitle: Embark on an exclusive trek up the highly coveted Huayna Picchu
itinerary.description:
Today you have the option to hike two different trails – Huayna Picchu or Machu Picchu Mountain, so it’s completely up to you! This will be the culmination of your Machu Picchu luxury tour, so enjoy it however you want. Adventurous travelers who desire something off-the-beaten-path should hike the steep slope of Huayna Picchu, offering unrivaled views of Machu Picchu. Please note that only a limited amount of hikers are allowed to climb Huayna Picchu each day and tickets will need to be purchased in advance along with your Machu Picchu entrance.

In the afternoon, reconvene in Aguas Calientes and board the return train to Ollantaytambo. Your Unu Raymi host will meet you at the station and bring you to your hotel for a well-earned evening of rest.

itinerary.title: DAY 6 - Cusco
itinerary.subtitle: Explore the Inca Capital and its culinary delights
itinerary.description:
Uncover the secrets of Cusco’s cobblestone streets and taste your wait through authentic Peruvian products.

Prepare to fall in love with Cusco, a gorgeous city that wins the heart of almost every traveler that passes through it. A private tour is the best way to learn about this historic city, and get the best insider secrets! After breakfast, meet your guide and wander among the archaeological remains of Sacsayhuaman, where the Incas staged a great battle against the conquistadors. Return to the city and venture through the bohemian neighborhood of San Blas, a hub of artistic inspiration. Explore Qoricancha and the Santo Domingo monastery, a colonial structure built on top of the ancient Inca temple of the sun. Live like a local and grab some groceries in the open-air San Pedro market for a delightful shopping experience!

At the end of the tour, your guide will suggest a few places to enjoy a delicious lunch, but be sure to save some room!

In the early afternoon, continue with your Peru culinary tour by heading to one of Cusco’s best restaurants and spending the afternoon learning about Peru’s culinary history and current cuisine from one of the best area chefs. You will learn how to make Peruvian starters and entrees, accompanied by a never-ending stream of snacks and samples fresh from the restaurant’s oven. Delight your palate with exotic fruits, make Pisco-based cocktails, learn a traditional way to slice vegetables, and spend the afternoon laughing and enjoying this truly special cooking class.

itinerary.title: DAY 7 - The Luxury Amazon Cruise Begins
itinerary.subtitle: Fly from Lima to Iquitos and board your luxury Amazon cruise
itinerary.description:
After breakfast at your hotel, we will escort you back to the airport for your flight to Iquitos before setting sail on the luxurious Delfin II ship. Upon arrival, you’ll meet your Delfin guide and take a seat for a scenic 90-minute drive to the small village of Nauta where the ship will be anchored.

Board the Delfin II and settle into a five-star cabin. After a safety drill and a quick briefing, tuck into a delicious welcome dinner and toast the beginning of your voyage with a glass of fine South American wine.

itinerary.title: DAY 8 - Enjoy Your Luxury Amazon Cruise
itinerary.subtitle: Your first day aboard the Delfin Luxury Cruise
itinerary.description:
On your first morning, getting up early is highly recommended! This enables you to appreciate one of the most important zones of the Pacaya Samiria National Reserve. Wildlife is most abundant and active with the rising of the sun, so you’ll have plenty of company to look for.

During the dry season (Jun-Nov), you will have the chance to do some hiking at Belluda Caño, where you can explore two different kinds of ecosystems: the “flooded forest” and the “terra firme” forest. Here you may see snail kites, black-tailed antbirds, manikins, tanagers, hummingbirds, woodpeckers, nun birds, orioles, blackbirds, and pygmy marmosets. Your hike will take you to a lagoon filled with endangered and unique freshwater fish, where you will explore the waters in a dugout canoe.

During the wet season (Dec-May), you will explore Belluda Cano Creek by skiff. Here you will get a chance to spot parrots, macaws, and monkeys. You may also see Morpho butterflies and various species of hawks, including the “laughing falcon,” named for its loud falsetto call.

This afternoon we’ll visit the Dorado River (“golden river”), where you might choose to go fishing for a piranha, a captivating and challenging experience you won’t forget! Or, you might want to go swimming with the delightful pink river dolphins, which some locals believe can transform into beautiful humans. These rare yet friendly creatures are mostly found in the freshwater rivers of the Amazon, near Iquitos. Make sure you bring your bathing suit and a waterproof camera! As night approaches, your guide will take you on a night safari in search of caiman alligators, nocturnal birds, and creepy crawlers.

itinerary.title: DAY 9 - Enjoy Your Luxury Amazon Cruise
itinerary.subtitle: Adventure through the Amazon Jungle
itinerary.description:
The morning is a perfect time for kayaking along the calm and inspiring rainforest waters of Zapote River. Your guides will take you upstream while you spot prehistoric-looking iguanas lying lazily in the sun. Travel along the shore and be ready for whatever the jungle has to offer. Squirrel monkeys are very active at this time of the day when they move in large noisy troops amongst the canopies.

In the afternoon, you will reach the Pacaya River at the heart of the Pacaya Samiria National Reserve, Peru’s largest protected area. This is by far the largest protected wetland reserve in the world, filled with lakes, palm swamps, and streams. The reserve becomes a flooded forest in the rainy season and is a highlight of any Amazon excursion. You will also have the chance to swim in one of the pristine lagoons in this wonderful region!

itinerary.title: DAY 10 - Enjoy Your Luxury Amazon Cruise
itinerary.subtitle: Adventure through the Amazon Jungle
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, climb aboard the aluminum skiff to explore Clavero Lake, where you will have a chance to venture deep into the rainforest and see a fantastic array of flora and fauna as local villagers paddle in their traditional canoes.

During the afternoon, you’ll have the opportunity to test your own skills on the water. First, you’ll sail to the Yarapa River on the skiffs, and then it’s into your very own kayak. Paddle through the tranquil waters, keeping an eye out for native flora and fauna at every turn! Next, you’ll visit the village of Puerto Miguel to meet local villagers who have called Amazonia their home for generations. Here, your naturalist guides will introduce you to village life in the jungle, and you’ll learn about native plants, local customs, and the seamless interaction between humans and wildlife.

Fall asleep for the last time under the Amazonian stars as the Delfin pull you back towards Iquitos.

itinerary.title: DAY 11 - Iquitos To Lima and Homebound
itinerary.subtitle: Explore a bit more of Iquitos before your flight home
itinerary.description:
After one final breakfast on the ship, you will arrive at the port of Nauta. The ground crew will be waiting to take you by private vehicle back to the city of Iquitos. As you journey back from Nauta to the Iquitos airport, you will stop at the Rescue & Rehabilitation Center of River Mammals (ACOBIA). Here, you will have the chance to meet baby manatees and learn about these wonderful, docile creatures, and why they are on the endangered species list!

Afterward, your guide will bring you to Iquitos airport for your return flight to Lima. In Lima, you will be met by an Unu Raymi host, who will escort you to Costa del Sol on-site airport hotel and will leave you to enjoy one final dinner in Peru before your international flight. Buen viaje!

tagline: La trilogía peruana: Selva Amazónica, Santuario de Machu Picchu y Lago Titicaca.
overview:
A fantasy adventure awaits with our Peru Amazon tours, combining the Amazon, Machu Picchu, and Lake Titicaca. From lush jungle canopies to Andean peaks, this journey showcases Peru’s stunning diversity.

Stay in a luxury eco-lodge in the Amazon, explore Machu Picchu’s ancient wonders, and sail the crystalline waters of Lake Titicaca. These Peru Amazon tours offer an unforgettable blend of nature, history, and culture.
inclusions: Personalized itinerary planning

The majority of meals in the itinerary
